Introduction and meaning
Cheating by personation. BNS restatement of IPC 416 / 419. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 416 / 419. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 319 is the rule on “Cheating by personation”. The section provides that (1) A person is said to cheat by personation if he cheats by pretending to be some other person, or by knowingly substituting one person for or another, or representing that he or any other person is a person other than he or such other person really is. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 319 exists so that “Cheating by personation” has a closed legal test in Chapter XVII — Of Offences Against Property. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Theft, snatching, extortion, robbery, dacoity, trust, cheating, mischief, trespass.

The provision in detail
319. (1) A person is said to cheat by personation if he cheats by pretending to be some other person, or by knowingly substituting one person for or another, or representing that he or any other person is a person other than he or such other person really is

(2) Whoever cheats by personation shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, or with fine, or with both

Of fraudulent deeds and dispositions of property

Essential ingredients
1. (1) A person is said to cheat by personation if he cheats by pretending to be some other person, or by knowingly substituting one person for or another, or representing that he or any other person is a person other than he or such other person really is
2. (2) Whoever cheats by personation shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, or with fine, or with both
3. Of fraudulent deeds and dispositions of property

Statutory illustrations
Illustration (a). A cheats by pretending to be a certain rich banker of the same name. A cheats by personation

Exam use: quote illustration (a), then write which ingredient of BNS s. 319 it proves. Copying the illustration without that mapping sentence does not score.

Illustration (b). A cheats by pretending to be B, a person who is deceased. A cheats by personation

Exam use: quote illustration (b), then write which ingredient of BNS s. 319 it proves. Copying the illustration without that mapping sentence does not score.

Explanations
Explanation.—The offence is committed whether the individual personated is a real or imaginary person

hypotheticals.question: Whether BNS s. 319 (Cheating by personation) applies, and how structured written arguments should be framed.
hypotheticals.analysis:
Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 319 (Cheating by personation), Chapter XVII — Of Offences Against Property.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) (1) A person is said to cheat by personation if he cheats by pretending to be some other person, or by knowingly substituting one person for or another, or representing that he or any other person is a person other than he or such other person really is
   (2) (2) Whoever cheats by personation shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, or with fine, or with both
   (3) Of fraudulent deeds and dispositions of property
Step 3 — Read every Explanation. An explanation is part of the section. Omitting it leaves the analysis incomplete and vulnerable to rebuttal.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 319 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.
